## Observation

In the last 40 failed CI runs (2026-10-23 to 2026-10-29), the `sweep (windows)` job failed `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_lifespan_drains_queued_events_on_shutdown` 27 times with `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests`. Other lifespan tests in that module fail the same way in the same runs, for example in run 40797257532:
- `test_lifespan_drain_is_bounded`
- `test_shutdown_completes_an_in_flight_store_write_and_releases_the_lock`
- `test_gerrit_internal_webhook_requires_the_gerrit_service_peer`

On Linux the same network attempt, `_current_revision` building a real `GerritClient`, is caught and the lookup fails open, so the error does not surface. Why it surfaces as the test failure on Windows has not been checked.

The same runs also show Windows-only failures unrelated to the network guard, for example `module 'signal' has no attribute 'SIGKILL'` and `State object has no attribute 'config'`.

## Plan
1. Read a Windows sweep log in full to find where the RuntimeError escapes, for example a call outside `_current_revision`'s try, or the reconcile loop.
2. Check whether eastmost-uncheered-nematode's default stub of `_current_revision` removes these failures on the next Windows sweep.
3. Fix the remaining escape, or skip POSIX-only tests on Windows the way fearful-valid-skua did, and give each skip its reason.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The point where the RuntimeError escapes on Windows is identified and recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] A scheduled `sweep (windows)` run after the fix shows no failure in tests/unit/test_review_bot.py. [non-codebase]
  provenance: the GitHub Actions run id and its result, recorded on this ticket.

## File impact (expected)
- tests/unit/test_review_bot.py
- tests/conftest.py
